correctness.rationale: For R=pi^{-1}tau, the initial relative permutation has k cycles and the terminal has 3k. A transposition splits or merges one cycle; any path has length 2k+2m where m is the merger count. Each of k disjoint untouched 3-cycle blocks must first be accessed from another block, necessarily by a merging swap, so m>=ceil(k/2). The displayed 6-move and 10-move templates are valid for respectively 2 and 3 blocks; decomposing k as sums of 2 and optionally 3 achieves the lower bound. Both finite scripts were executed, including exhaustive BFS for n=6,9, but only the constructive proof establishes all k.

originality.rationale: The same derangement-transposition graph, its connectivity and certain local or spanning-walk features were studied previously and are not claimed as new. Full-text and scholarly-record comparisons identified no theorem yielding this exact pairwise inverse-three-cycle flip distance for every k>=2 or its unbounded additive gap. Distinctive new implication is a tight first-touch merging bound matched by bounded-size switch templates across an infinite family. Unindexed equivalent results remain a risk.
residual_risks: A historically equivalent derivation might be indexed under forbidden-position permutation sorting, derangement swap routing, or crown-graph reconfiguration rather than the searched terminology.

value.rationale: The forbidden diagonal in a crown graph makes four-cycle matching-switch routing genuinely different from ordinary transposition sorting. This theorem quantifies a sharp unbounded additive distance penalty for a canonical infinite family of inverse cycle-products, with an explanatory first-touch merging invariant and matching constructive routes. It is relevant to shortest paths and local mixing geometry, not a routine state-count calculation.
